chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (the second Imam, peace be upon him) in the year in which he performed Hajj, and that was the year 212 AH, and I said, 'May I be your ransom, by what did you enter Mecca, as Mufrid or as Mutamatti?' He said, 'As Mutamatti.' I said, 'Which is better: the Tamattu' of Umrah to Hajj, or the one who performs Hajj as Mufrid and brings the offering?' He said, 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: The Tamattu' of Umrah to Hajj is better than the Mufrid who brings the offering.' And he used to say, 'The pilgrim does not enter with anything better than the Tamattu'.'

And it is not for anyone to say that what you have cited from these hadiths regarding the Mutamatti being better than the Mufrid and the Qarin invalidates what you mentioned first, that whoever performed Hajj as Mufrid or Qarin did not fulfill the obligation of Hajj of Islam, and to say that if it were not fulfilling, then Tamattu' would not be better than it. For we, even if we say that the obligatory act is Tamattu' and that nothing else fulfills the discharge of liability, did not say that the Mufrid or the Qarin is disobedient to Allah, Exalted is He. For whoever performs Hajj as Mufrid or Qarin, he deserves abundant reward even if the obligation does not fall from him.

And the analogy of that is that whoever is obliged to perform an obligatory prayer and performs a voluntary prayer, he deserves reward for it even if the voluntary prayer does not fulfill the obligatory one. And similarly, whoever is obliged to pay obligatory Zakat on a known amount, and gives something from his wealth as voluntary charity, he deserves reward for that even if the Zakat remains in his liability.

And is he one who has fulfilled the Hajj of Islam, or one who has not? And it is permissible that what is meant by it is one who fulfilled the Hajj of Islam then performed Hajj voluntarily, for he is free to choose to perform Hajj as Mutamatti, or Qarin, or Mufrid, and he deserves reward for every type of them, even if what he deserves through Tamattu' is greater.
As for the report that he narrated,

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)
key_terms.اَلْقَارِنُ: Al-Qarin (one who performs Umrah and Hajj together)
key_terms.اَلْمُفْرِدُ: Al-Mufrid (one who performs Hajj alone without Umrah)
key_terms.اَلْهَدْيُ: Al-Hady (sacrificial animal brought by the pilgrim)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Mutamatti, Mufrid, and Qarin in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* records Imam al-Sadiq’s preference for Tamattu' as the optimal form of Hajj, distinguishing its superior reward from the validity of Mufrid and Qarin forms. The scholar elaborates that while Tamattu' is the primary obligation, the other forms are not invalid but rather yield distinct rewards, analogous to how voluntary prayers or extra charity do not negate the primary duty yet still merit divine favor.
